sections.title: Repository Folder Hierarchy
sections.content:
To ensure VenvHub Pro discovers your development codebases and maintains USB portability, proper root organization is required.

A. Set Root Path:
Open Settings -> Root Paths -> Local Packages (pip -e) and pick your root development directory.

B. Directory Separation (Recommended):
Keep standard Linker packages separated from pip -e source trees:

└── local_packages/
    ├── linker/    (packages containing local_meta.json)
    └── pip_e/     (packages containing setup.py / pyproject.toml)
Portable Mode Requirement: In portable USB workflows, your source directories must reside on the same drive as VenvHub Pro. Storing packages on the desktop breaks path resolution on secondary machines.

sections.title: Installing & Linking Editable Packages
sections.content:
Linking local source packages into virtual environments:

  1. Open Venv Manager.
  2. Right-click the target virtual environment row.
  3. Select ✏️ Local Packages (pip -e).
  4. Click ➕ Install from Folder (pip -e).
  5. Select the root folder of your module containing setup.py or pyproject.toml.

Pip (or UV) links the package into the active environment without copying files, creating a live bridge directly to your source code.

Tip: If the installer prompts that no build descriptor was found, ensure you selected the root directory rather than an internal src/ subdirectory.

sections.title: Runtime Behavior & Native VS Code IntelliSense
sections.content:
Post-installation lifecycle mechanics:

  • A. Dependency Resolution: Pip inspects pyproject.toml and downloads required upstream PyPI packages automatically into the Venv.
  • B. Link File (.pth/.egg-link): Creates a path pointer inside site-packages referencing your live source folder.
  • C. Native IDE Resolution: Unlike the Linker module, pip -e registers directly in site-packages. Pylance in VS Code natively indexes the module without modifying settings.json. IntelliSense and Go-to-Definition (F12) work automatically out-of-the-box.

sections.title: USB Portability & Automated Path Self-Healing
sections.content:
When USB drive letters change across workstations (e.g. E:\ at home to F:\ at work), standard Pip .pth files break because they contain hardcoded absolute paths, causing ModuleNotFoundError.

How VenvHub Pro Auto-Heals Broken Paths

Upon every execution launch, the PortablePathLogic engine runs in milliseconds:

  1. Detects previous drive letter binding from Venv metadata (e.g. E:).
  2. Resolves the current physical drive letter (e.g. F:).
  3. Scans site-packages for all .pth and .egg-link references.
  4. Silently rewrites drive letter bindings across all link files.
Automated Healing Matrix:
ScenarioAuto-Healed?
Entire stack (Project + Venv + Source) moves on same USB drive (E: → F:)Yes – matches physical drive UUID
Copied to a different physical disk (different UUID)No – relink via ➕ button
Only source folder moved independently of VenvNo – healing tracks Venv disk

sections.title: Uninstalling & Detaching Packages
sections.content:
Removing editable packages from an environment:

  1. Open ✏️ Local Packages (pip -e).
  2. Select the package from the table.
  3. Click ❌ Uninstall Selected.

VenvHub executes pip uninstall -y <package> and purges link descriptors from site-packages immediately.

sections.title: Critical Best Practices & Warnings
sections.content:
Do Not Combine Linker and Pip -e on the Same Package!
Never link a single directory simultaneously via 'Local Packages (Linker)' and 'Pip -e'. Conflicting import hooks and .pth files will trigger unpredictable namespace collisions.

sections.title: Configuring pyproject.toml
sections.content:
Minimal functional pyproject.toml for editable packages:

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "my-test-package"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Package overview"
dependencies = []

Flat Layout Architecture (Simplest)

my_package/
├── pyproject.toml
└── my_test/            <- folder name = import name
    ├── __init__.py
    └── greeting.py

Src Layout Architecture

my_package/
├── pyproject.toml
└── src/
    └── my_test/         <- subfolder inside src/
        ├── __init__.py
        └── greeting.py
Common Pitfall: Placing __init__.py directly in src/ rather than src/my_test/ causes package discovery to fail with ModuleNotFoundError.

sections.title: Chained Local Dependencies (pip1 → pip2)
sections.content:
When developing interdependent local libraries where pip2 imports from pip1, install packages in sequential order.

Recommended Directory Structure

pip_e/
├── pip1/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── my_test/
│       ├── __init__.py
│       └── greeting.py
└── pip2/
    ├── pyproject.toml
    └── my_tool/
        ├── __init__.py
        └── helper.py       <- imports "from my_test import hello"
Do Not Add Local Package Names to dependencies!
Adding unreleased local names to dependencies causes Pip to query PyPI, failing the installation. Install local modules sequentially instead.

Installation Pipeline:

  1. In 'Local Packages (pip -e)', install pip1 first.
  2. Install dependent pip2 next.
  3. Confirm both packages appear active in the matrix.
